note: All regex patterns target Google Search Console's query filter, which is evaluated with RE2 syntax (no lookahead/lookbehind, no backreferences). Every pattern here is written to be RE2-safe. GSC query strings are normalized lowercase, so patterns are written lowercase throughout. Each preset also carries a difficulty rating and tags for filtering.

presets.name: 5W1H Questions
presets.description: Queries starting with who, what, when, where, why, how.
examples: how to fix a leaking tap
presets.useCase: Surfaces question-shaped queries for FAQ pages, featured snippets, and AEO content.
presets.notes: Anchored to start of string; won't catch mid-sentence questions like 'tips on how to...' — use the individual question presets below for that.

presets.name: Yes / No Questions
presets.description: Queries starting with a yes/no question auxiliary (can, should, does, is, are, will, do).
presets.useCase: Good for direct-answer content blocks and schema FAQ markup.
presets.notes: May include some non-question uses of 'is'/'are' at the start of a phrase; spot check results.

presets.name: "How To" Queries
presets.description: Instructional queries using the exact phrase 'how to'.
examples: how to fix a leaking tap
presets.useCase: Dedicated tutorial and step-by-step guide content; strong candidate for HowTo schema.

presets.name: "What Is" Queries
presets.description: Definitional questions using 'what is' or 'what are'.
presets.useCase: Definition-first content and glossary pages targeting the definition snippet box.

presets.name: Beginner / For Beginners
presets.useCase: Entry-level guide and onboarding content opportunities.

presets.name: "Why" Questions (General)
presets.description: Any query starting with 'why', not limited to diagnostic/problem phrasing.
examples: why do businesses need a website
presets.useCase: Explainer and thought-leadership content; feeds AEO reasoning-style answers.
presets.notes: Overlaps in theme with 'Why Is X ___' in Problem Queries, but that one is scoped to diagnostic/failure phrasing anywhere in the query; this one is anchored to the start and covers general reasoning questions too.

presets.name: "Can I" Queries
presets.description: Queries containing the specific phrase 'can i', anywhere in the string.
examples: can i claim this on tax
can i install solar panels myself
can i return this without a receipt
presets.useCase: Permission/eligibility-style questions; great for policy and terms-clarification content.

presets.name: "Which" Queries
presets.description: Queries starting with 'which', typically choosing between options.
examples: which crm is best for startups
which credit card has no fees
presets.useCase: Decision-support and buyer's-guide content that helps narrow a shortlist.

presets.name: "Where" Queries
presets.description: Queries starting with 'where', usually seeking a location or source.
examples: where can i watch this movie
where do i download this app
presets.useCase: Locator and sourcing content; complements the Local SEO category for physical-location intent.

presets.name: FAQ / Frequently Asked
presets.description: Queries explicitly referencing an FAQ or common-questions format.
presets.useCase: Direct signal to build or expand a dedicated FAQ page with schema markup.

presets.name: "When" Questions
examples: when is the best time to post on instagram
when should i replace my tyres
when do i need to renew my passport
presets.useCase: Timing-sensitive content, seasonal guides, and scheduling advice pages.

presets.name: "Who" Questions
presets.description: Queries asking about a person, company, or entity behind something.
examples: who is the ceo of this company
presets.useCase: Attribution, about-us, and founder/company-story content opportunities.

presets.name: "Best" Queries
presets.description: Queries containing 'best', a strong commercial-investigation signal.
presets.useCase: Identify roundup/listicle and category-page opportunities.
presets.notes: Combine with the Local SEO category to isolate 'best X near me' queries.

presets.name: "Top N" Queries
presets.useCase: Roundup content and comparison-table opportunities.
presets.notes: \d* allows 'top' alone or 'top 10'; tighten to \d+ if you only want numbered lists.

presets.name: Most Popular

presets.name: Complaints / Scam Checks

presets.notes: '.*' inside the group can be slow on very large query sets in some regex engines, but is fine under RE2.

presets.name: "Near Me"
presets.useCase: Location page and Google Business Profile content prioritization.

presets.name: "In [City]" Pattern
presets.description: Queries with an explicit local qualifier using 'in'.
presets.useCase: Surfaces city-specific query variants for location-page targeting.
presets.notes: GSC query strings are lowercase, so this pattern uses a lowercase character class rather than [A-Z].

presets.name: Open Now / Opening Hours
presets.useCase: Google Business Profile hours accuracy and 'open now' landing content.

presets.name: Directions
examples: how do i get to the airport

presets.name: County / Region

presets.name: Service / Delivery Area

examples: do you deliver to my area

presets.name: Closest / Nearest

examples: what is the location of this office

presets.name: Within X Miles / Minutes
presets.useCase: Radius-based store-locator tools and coverage-area content.

presets.name: City, State Pair
presets.useCase: US multi-location landing page targeting by city/state combination.
presets.notes: Broad character class; may match unrelated comma-separated text. Spot-check matches before acting on them.

presets.name: Nationwide / Across the Country
presets.description: Broad-coverage local-service queries (opposite end of the local spectrum).
presets.useCase: National-coverage messaging for multi-location or shipping-based businesses.

presets.name: Guide / Tutorial / Tips
presets.useCase: Blog and resource-hub content planning.

presets.description: Queries asking what a term means.

presets.name: List Of

examples: step by step guide to meditation

presets.useCase: Explainer and pillar-content opportunities.

examples: how does a heat pump work

presets.name: Reset / Reinstall / Clear Cache

presets.name: Virus / Hacked / Malware

presets.name: Current Year / "Latest"
presets.description: Freshness-seeking queries referencing a year or recency.
presets.useCase: Flags pages needing a freshness/date update, or content gaps for year-specific roundups.
presets.notes: Year range covers 2026-2035; update periodically. Consider a settings-driven year variable in a future version.

presets.name: Recent Changes / Announcements
presets.description: Queries about a recent change, update, or announcement.
presets.useCase: News-style or changelog content opportunities.
presets.notes: Overlaps with 'Current Year / Latest'; kept separate since not every freshness query names a year.

presets.name: This Year / Current Year
presets.description: Relative-time freshness phrasing that doesn't name a specific year.
presets.useCase: Evergreen-but-time-sensitive content that needs an annual refresh cycle.

presets.name: Updated For / Revised
presets.description: Queries seeking a version updated for current standards or rules.
presets.useCase: Signals content that should carry a visible 'last updated' date.

presets.name: New Release / Just Released
presets.useCase: Launch-announcement and early-adopter content.

presets.name: Latest Version / Newest Model
presets.useCase: Version-comparison and release-note content.

presets.name: Seasonal / This Month / Next Season
presets.useCase: Seasonal-campaign and time-boxed promotional content.

presets.name: Brand Queries
presets.description: Matches any query containing your brand name(s). Set your brand name(s) on the card below — no regex editing needed.
presets.useCase: Isolate branded search demand from non-branded demand; combine with the Non-Brand category to see the split.
presets.notes: The {{brand}} token is filled in from the "Your brand name(s)" field on this card (comma-separate multiple spellings, e.g. Acme, Acme Inc, Acme Co). Saved per-browser and reused everywhere this preset appears.

presets.name: Brand + Common Modifier
presets.description: Brand queries paired with a frequent post-modifier like reviews, login, or support.
presets.useCase: Reveals what searchers most often attach to your brand name, informing navigational-page and support-content priorities.
presets.notes: Uses the same {{brand}} token as the other Brand presets.

presets.name: Brand Navigational Intent
presets.description: Brand queries seeking a specific destination: site, hours, or phone number.
presets.useCase: Confirms navigational branded demand is being satisfied by your homepage, GBP listing, and sitelinks.

presets.name: Brand vs Competitor
presets.description: Queries directly comparing your brand against an unnamed competitor using 'vs'.
presets.useCase: Surfaces competitive-comparison demand for dedicated 'us vs them' comparison pages.
presets.notes: Combine with the Comparison category's 'X vs Y' preset for the full comparison-query picture.

presets.name: Brand + Any Product Word (Broad)
presets.description: Broad catch-all for your brand name followed by any single word.
presets.useCase: Broad branded-demand sweep to spot emerging query patterns before they justify their own preset.
presets.notes: Deliberately broad; use the Result History view to periodically review what's showing up here.

presets.name: Generic / Non-Brand Starter (Reference Only)
presets.description: Anti-pattern reference: an attempt to isolate non-brand queries by excluding your brand terms.
presets.useCase: Documents why brand-exclusion regex doesn't work in GSC, and points to the supported alternative.
presets.notes: IMPORTANT: this pattern uses a negative-lookahead idiom '(?!...)' which is NOT supported by RE2, the engine GSC's custom regex filter actually runs on. It will fail to apply in Search Console. Kept here only as a reference/anti-pattern; use the 'Exclude' side of GSC's built-in query filter (Query does not contain) for brand exclusion instead of regex.

presets.name: Generic Category Terms
presets.description: Positively matches generic, category-style descriptors rather than trying to exclude your brand.
presets.useCase: A working alternative to brand-exclusion: since RE2 can't express 'does not contain', this positively captures generic/category-style demand instead. Pair with GSC's built-in 'Query does not contain' filter for a true brand-exclusion split.

presets.name: Other Superlatives
presets.description: Superlative adjectives beyond 'best' (worst, fastest, easiest, etc).
presets.useCase: Captures superlative-driven roundup and ranking content beyond the 'best' preset.
presets.notes: Deliberately excludes 'best' since that's already covered by the Commercial Intent category's dedicated preset.

presets.name: Free
presets.useCase: Freemium/lead-magnet content and free-tier landing pages.

presets.name: DIY / Do It Yourself
presets.useCase: Self-service tutorial content, distinct from professional-service-seeking queries.

presets.name: Online
presets.useCase: Digital-channel content and remote-service positioning.

presets.name: In-Person / In-Store
presets.useCase: In-store/physical-visit content and click-and-collect messaging.

presets.name: Quick / Fast
examples: quick fix for a flat tyre
presets.useCase: Speed-focused messaging and time-saving content angles.

presets.name: Easy / Simple
presets.useCase: Simplified/low-barrier content angle, distinct from the dedicated 'for beginners' phrasing.
presets.notes: Some overlap with the Questions category's 'Beginner' preset; this one targets the broader adjective usage, not just the 'for beginners' phrase.

presets.name: For [Audience]
presets.useCase: Audience-specific landing pages and segmented content strategy.

presets.name: Size Modifiers
presets.useCase: Size-variant product filtering and category-page faceting.

presets.name: Number + Ways / Steps / Tips
presets.useCase: Numbered-listicle content, a well-tested featured-snippet and CTR format.

presets.name: Percentage Value
presets.description: Queries referencing an explicit percentage figure.
presets.useCase: Promotion-percentage and statistic-driven content, useful for tracking discount-query volume.

presets.name: Without / No ___ Needed
presets.description: Queries expressing a constraint or exclusion in the searcher's own need.
examples: credit card with no annual fee needed
presets.useCase: Constraint-based content that addresses a specific limitation or requirement gap.

presets.useCase: B2B/bulk-order pricing pages and wholesale-account signup content.

presets.useCase: Sustainability-focused product lines and green-messaging content.

presets.name: Custom / Personalized / Bespoke
presets.useCase: Customization-service pages and personalized-product configurators.

presets.name: Portable / Mobile / Wireless
presets.useCase: Feature-specific product filtering for mobility-focused categories.

presets.name: Short-Tail Keywords (1-2 Words)
presets.description: Queries made up of only one or two words — broad, high-volume, high-competition "head" terms.
presets.useCase: Identify high-volume head-term queries for competitive analysis, pillar-page targeting, and category-page optimization.
presets.notes: Anchored to the full query string, so it correctly excludes anything with a 3rd word rather than just checking for the presence of 1-2 words somewhere.

presets.name: Mid-Tail Keywords (3 Words)
presets.description: Queries made up of exactly three words — the middle ground between broad head terms and specific long-tail phrases.
presets.useCase: Balance-point queries with decent volume and moderate competition — good candidates for subcategory or comparison pages.

presets.name: Long-Tail Keywords (4+ Words)
presets.description: Queries made up of four or more words — specific, lower-competition "long-tail" phrases.
examples: best running shoes for flat feet
how to fix a leaking bathroom tap myself
affordable seo agency for small local business
what is the difference between shared and vps hosting
cheapest way to ship a package internationally
presets.useCase: Surface long-tail query opportunities, typically easier to rank for and often higher-converting due to their specificity.
presets.notes: {3,} means '3 or more repetitions of word+space', followed by one final word — i.e. 4+ words total. RE2 supports bounded/unbounded repetition natively; this is not a lookaround construct.

presets.name: Extra-Long-Tail / Conversational (6+ Words)
presets.description: Queries made up of six or more words — often conversational, voice-search, or AI-chat-style phrasing.
examples: what is the best way to remove a red wine stain from carpet
how much does it cost to replace a car windshield in the uk
can i return an online order without the original packaging
what should i look for when buying a used car privately
is it cheaper to lease or buy a car for business use
presets.useCase: Captures ultra-specific, conversational queries increasingly common with voice search and AI assistants — a strong AEO/conversational-content signal, and usually the lowest-competition tier of all.

presets.name: Video Intent
presets.description: Queries likely to trigger or want a video result.
examples: how to tie a tie video
video guide to changing a tyre
presets.useCase: Video-content and video-schema opportunities to compete for the video pack.

presets.name: Image / Visual Intent
presets.description: Queries likely to trigger or want an image result.
presets.useCase: Optimized imagery, alt text, and image-sitemap opportunities to compete for the image pack.

presets.name: Downloadable Asset Intent
presets.useCase: Gated-content and downloadable-asset lead-magnet opportunities.
